title: Memory-Aware Agent Harnesses for Anti-Money Laundering — Nacho Martinez, Oracle
talk_summary: Speaker presents an agent harness workshop for AML, emphasizing that the harness/data layer—memory, context engineering, tool/skill retrieval, agent loop—matters more than swapping frontier models. He demonstrates vectorized skill/tool retrieval, context summarization/compaction, memory tiers, and pre-approved SQL tools to keep context small and agents reliable.

takeaways.what_they_do: They embed tools and skills in vector stores and retrieve only the top few relevant ones per request instead of injecting the full catalog into context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you create vector embeddings out of the tools and out of the skills... pull the most relevant skill or tool
takeaways.numbers: 100 skills; 3k-5k tokens per skill; default top 3; tools/skills ~80% of request; Pi ~6k vs others 30-40k initial tokens

takeaways.what_they_do: They summarize or chunk old conversation into DB/files with IDs/offsets, then let the agent pull chunks back only when needed.
takeaways.numbers: workshop loop max 8 iterations and 60s reasoning per iteration

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep short-term context separate from long-term episodic/procedural/semantic memory and promote only valuable items from a run into long-term storage for later recall.
takeaways.evidence_quote: worth keeping, you promote it to the long-term memory

takeaways.what_they_do: They expose vetted, pre-created SQL queries through MCP/tools so agents don't generate dialect-specific SQL from scratch and hallucinate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: pre-create some SQL queries and then let the agents access those... proven to work

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue shared mutable files need transactional/ACID semantics; worktrees are a workaround for multi-agent write consistency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you had transactional consistency or acid consistency... you would not get this issue

takeaways.what_they_do: They cap the agent loop by max iterations and reasoning time, and tailor harness constraints to the problem.
takeaways.evidence_quote: maximum number of iterations in our case will be eight and a maximum of 60 seconds of reasoning
